participant.title: Storage bucket for Riverside Physiotherapy Clinic
participant.scenario: Riverside Physiotherapy Clinic scans the referral letters it receives from doctors and wants to keep them in cloud storage. You look after the clinic's IT. Create the storage bucket riverside-referral-letters. The form has been pre-filled with the settings copied from the clinic's old bucket, which hosts its public website.

requirements.text: The letters contain patient information. Nobody outside the clinic may read them: block all public access to the bucket.
The letters must be encrypted at rest.
Earlier versions of each letter must be kept, so that a letter deleted or overwritten by mistake can be recovered.
Every request made to the bucket must be logged to the clinic's existing log bucket, riverside-access-logs.

participant.notes: The bucket name and region are already correct.

display.title: Online storage for Riverside Physiotherapy Clinic
display.scenario: Riverside Physiotherapy Clinic scans the referral letters it receives from doctors and wants to keep them online. You look after the clinic's computers. Set up a storage space called riverside-referral-letters using the form below. The form is already filled in with the settings copied from the clinic's old storage space, which holds its public website.

requirements.text: The letters contain patient information. Nobody outside the clinic may read them: block all public access.
The letters must be encrypted (scrambled so that they cannot be read without a key).
Earlier versions of each letter must be kept, so that a letter deleted or overwritten by mistake can be recovered.
Every time someone uses this storage space, a record must be saved in the clinic's existing records storage, riverside-access-logs.

display.notes: The storage name and location are already correct.

traps.basis: The old bucket serves a public website through a public bucket policy, which only works with the two policy-related Block Public Access settings switched off. The real S3 console can copy settings from an existing bucket when a new one is created. Both switches must be turned back on to pass ST-01.
Server access logging is off on new S3 buckets until it is switched on (Security Hub S3.9 flags this).
